facts.fact: Bikan scenery includes white-walled storehouses, namako walls and willows beside the Kurashiki River.
facts.excerpt: Japanese-style storehouses with white walls, namako walls, and rows of willows

facts.fact: The canal once carried goods; optional boat tickets are sold by Kurashiki-kan, not included in a self-guided waterfront walk.
facts.excerpt: The Kurashiki River once bustled with boats carrying goods.
facts.location: Punting Boat Rides on Kuashiki River

facts.fact: Boat operation has seasonal closure rules and is not available on every winter weekday; consult rather than promising a sailing.
facts.excerpt: January to February: Operated only on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays
facts.location: Punting Boat Rides on Kuashiki River

facts.fact: Kurashiki-kan was built as the town hall in1917 and now has tourist information, a rest space, multipurpose toilets and lockers.
facts.excerpt: built as Kurashiki Town Hall in 1917

facts.fact: Ivy Square reuses the Kurashiki Spinning Works factory; the complex includes red-brick buildings, a pottery studio, hotel and Kurabo Memorial Hall.
facts.excerpt: The square is a complex completed by renovating the factory of Kurashiki Spinning works.

facts.fact: Kurabo Memorial Hall introduces spinning history and has its own admission arrangements; courtyard viewing is separate from entry to exhibition facilities.
facts.excerpt: Kurabo Memorial Hall introduces the history of the spinning industry.
facts.location: Kurashiki Ivy Square / Kurabo Memorial Hall

facts.fact: Ohara has Western paintings alongside modern Japanese work, crafts and Asian antiquities; not every named artwork is promised on display.
facts.excerpt: modern and contemporary Japanese artworks, and Oriental and Eastern antiquities.
